newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's aluminum sector narrows losses.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's aluminum sector narrows losses.

text.p: Venezuela's state-owned aluminum sector, due to be privatized on Jan 31, narrowed its debt to 25.967 billion bolivars in 1996, from 112.970 billion bolivars in 1995, according to official figures obtained by Reuters.
Of the four companies only smelter Alcasa and bauxite/alumina producer Bauxilum registered losses. Smelter Venalum, and carbon anode producer Carbonorca registered small profits, the figures showed.
"Alcasa and Bauxilum registered losses due to the great weight of their debts," the report of state holding Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) said.

Alcasa is expected to make a loss of 30.812 billion bolivars in 1996, compared to 59,078 billion in 1995. Bauxilum will make a loss of 19.972 billion bolivars compared to 62.971 billion bolivars last year.

Venalum, meanwhile, will make a profit of 23.626 billion bolivars, up from 8,407 billion bolivars in 1995. Carbonorca's profits were seen rising to 1.191 billion bolivars from 872 million bolivars last year.

Of the four companies, only Alcasa has reduced its staff in 1996, to 3,003, from 3,013 in 1995. Baluxilum's staff increased to 2,703 from 2,564, Carbonorca's to 465, from 431 and Venalum's from 3,141 to 2,956.

Thirteen companies have qualified to bid for a controlling stake in the four-company sector including Aluminum Company of America (Alcoa), Gencor Ltd, Glencore Ltdu, Reynolds Metals Co, Norsk Hydro ASA, and RTZ Corp-Cra Ltd.
